headline: High: Claude Code can write shared files/git while Rasa can ingest external chat inputs, creating default-path prompt, data, and action-cascade risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read/write repo files and shared filesystem state, and its outputs can be consumed through files or MCP. Rasa ingests text from external channels like Slack/Telegram, so if Claude Code writes attacker-controlled instructions into shared artifacts, Rasa may treat them as dialogue content. The pairwise bridge is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF Claude Code writes prompts or instructions into a file that Rasa later reads as conversation content
IF Rasa is configured to ingest shared workspace text without provenance filtering
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all inter-agent files
Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Disable file-based handoff between agents
Review any shared message queue or webhook payloads before ingestion
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the Rasa boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, while Rasa handles text and voice and can send data over allowlisted network paths. If they share a workspace or handoff files, sensitive code or secrets from Claude Code can flow into Rasa outputs or upstream channels. The leakage path is inferred from the profiles, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or ticket attachments
IF Rasa forwards conversation content to external messaging APIs containing shared file excerpts
mitigations: Move sensitive repos to a separate directory
Restrict Rasa to redacted inputs only
Turn off automatic attachment ingestion
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code has filesystem write, git modification, shell execution, and broad egress; Rasa can also interact with external channels and has allowlisted egress. Overlap on mutable resources can cause conflicting writes or inconsistent state if both touch the same repo, ticket, or integration target. No locking is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same git branch or working tree
IF both agents post to the same external integration endpoint without coordination
mitigations: Assign separate branches or directories
Serialize writes through one operator
Pause one agent during commits or deployments
Use a lockfile around shared resources
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks to shared targets

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code, shell commands, and file edits that Rasa may later surface or act on through conversational workflows. Rasa is a dialogue system, so if it treats Claude Code output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into user-facing responses or downstream actions. Because the verification boundary is not documented, the safer higher severity is high.
conditions: IF Rasa uses Claude Code-generated text as a source for replies or automation
IF no human or programmatic verification step exists between Claude Code output and Rasa action
mitigations: Require human review before publishing outputs
Add schema validation for any handoff payload
Compare Claude Code outputs against source files before use
Limit Rasa to templated responses for shared tasks
requires-engineering: add verification gates and provenance tracking

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code explicitly handles git credentials and shell environment data, while Rasa handles text/voice and can relay content through third-party messaging APIs. If regulated or personal data is placed into shared workflows, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this remains medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed from Claude Code into Rasa channels
IF the deployment uses messaging providers with retention policies that differ from the source system
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared prompts
Document retention for each messaging channel
Mask secrets before handoff
Restrict Rasa channels to approved jurisdictions
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and deletion workflows
